source.title: An Investigation of Why Overparameterization Exacerbates Spurious Correlations
source.authors: Shiori Sagawa; Aditi Raghunathan; Pang Wei Koh; Percy Liang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or corruption affecting the study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies model size and reports training classification error alongside worst-group test error on image and synthetic datasets. This bears directly on whether increasing model size reaches zero training error, though its central question is the resulting worst-group generalization.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's reported results about training error across model sizes and procedures. ERM appendix text gives numeric training-error outcomes only for selected model sizes; main-text plots describe the training-error pattern but do not provide recoverable values. Cited results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The CelebA experiments extend V1's convolutional-network training-error question to a new dataset: widening ResNet10 trained with SGD yields zero training error. Waterbirds and synthetic experiments optimize logistic regression with L-BFGS and do not test the system and optimizer named in V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors find that overparameterization can worsen worst-group generalization under spurious correlations, with group imbalance and relative feature informativeness governing the synthetic results. They propose an inductive bias toward less memorization and show that majority subsampling can improve worst-group performance. Zero training error under weak regularization and nonzero error under strong regularization are experimental observations, rather than the paper's central conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies model width or random-feature count and measures group-wise classification errors under reweighted, ERM, and subsampled objectives; it does not test the cited CIFAR random-label memorization recipe. ResNet10 uses SGD with momentum; Waterbirds and synthetic tasks use logistic regression over random projections.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-error outcomes vary with regularization: strong L2 regularization (λ = 0.1) prevents zero training error even in overparameterized models. The datasets and training objectives also differ across reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Waterbirds and synthetic random-feature logistic-regression models reach zero training error at sufficiently large feature counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the number of fixed random features can allow logistic regression optimized with L-BFGS to interpolate training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Overparameterization can worsen worst-group test error despite zero training error; majority subsampling can improve worst-group generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation and improved average generalization can coexist with poor minority-group generalization under spurious correlations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The directly stated training-error outcomes are selective rather than a complete numeric sweep. Some outcomes are described qualitatively or appear only in plots. The paper notes worst-group error can be unstable across epochs because of small sample size and relatively large learning rate; it reports averages over the last 10 epochs.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only training-error series for model-size sweeps in Figures 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, and 12 were not individually extracted because exact values are not given in the text and would require reading plots. Training error for some ERM sweeps is not numerically reported.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and early stopping are untested. Random initialization is not explicitly established. Strongly regularized CelebA training error is not quantified, so substantial error is not established.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum experiment or extra-student-neuron comparison.
No depth sweep or comparison of plain and residual networks.
No initialization comparison or measurement of initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.
No stability-threshold, curvature, catapult, or edge-of-stability measurement.
Batch normalization is used without a comparison against training without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. CelebA supplies a new-setting test of V1, while logistic-regression interpolation does not establish convolutional-network optimization. Nonzero error under strong regularization is already anticipated by V1 and therefore does not warrant limits_scope. Figure-only sweeps are declared in rows_left_out; no additional readable V1 result requires a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, or Adam; tests CelebA, Waterbirds, and synthetic data, including stated SGD training for ResNet10.
